newsitem.title: USA: Hot, dry week stresses South Dakota row crops.
newsitem.headline: Hot, dry week stresses South Dakota row crops.

text.p: A hot, dry week enabled producers to begin small grain harvest, but row crops and pastures were stressed by the heat and lack of moisture, the Agricultural Statistics Service reported.

The winter wheat crop was eight percent harvested as of Sunday, down from 15 percent on average. The crop was rated one percent very poor, seven percent poor, 34 percent fair, 50 percent good and eight percent excellent.
Spring wheat was rated one percent very poor, six percent poor, 23 percent fair, 51 percent good and 19 percent excellent.
The crop was turning color on half the acreage, up from 46 percent for the five-year average. One percent was ripe, against the seven percent average.
Soybeans were blooming on 33 percent of the acreage, against 35 percent on average, while pods were set on seven percent, versus the three percent average.
Corn was tasselling on eight percent of the acreage, against 15 percent on average. Corn was rated one percent very poor, five poor, 18 fair, 53 good and 23 percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated five percent very short, 30 percent short, 61 percent adequate and four percent surplus.
